Metrics.ElementText:
One Recovery Bucks offers advice and information to support you to reduce the harm caused by alcohol misuse. They offer a range of support aimed at reducing harm and improving your health. The service is free and confidential to residents of Buckinghamshire aged 18 and over affected by their own or someone else’s alcohol use. One Recovery Bucks offer a wide range of treatments and interventions to individuals using their services. You will be allocated a keyworker and together you will identify what your needs and goals are and how they can best support you.  

Services available:
• Harm reduction services: naloxone, needle exchange, safer injecting advice, sexual health services, blood-borne virus (BBV) testing & vaccination
• Outreach services
• Brief interventions and advice for those not seeking structured treatment
• Self-help resources and online support
• Supportive, clinical treatment prescribing programmes (for opiates and alcohol) for detox and relapse prevention
• Referral into inpatient detoxification or stabilisation and residential rehabilitation
• Psycho-social one-to-one and group work interventions (check timetable to ask in the hub)
• Individualised treatment care plans for all illicit drugs and alcohol including new psychoactive substances (formerly known as legal highs)
• Evidenced-based therapeutic interventions
• Support and treatment for prescription-only medication drugs (POM) and over-the-counter drugs (OTC) 
• Complementary therapies
• Group activities
• Health promotion including sexual health advice and contraception
• Intensive aftercare support packages
• Comprehensive recovery service and activities 
• Diversionary activities
• Volunteering programme
• Online recovery resources
• Recovery mentor support 
• Mutual aid
Monday, Tuesday, Thursday, Friday 9am - 5pm, Wednesday 9am - 8pm
Buckinghamshire
Self referral or via other professional.

Services.ServiceName: Alcohol addiction - support for family and friends

Metrics.ElementText:
Change Grow Live Manchester work with anyone looking to make positive changes related to drug & alcohol use. We approach treatment with an open mind, free from judgement. If your goals don't include treatment and recovery, but you do want to reduce the harmful impacts of drug & alcohol use, we can help with this too.  

Change Grow Live are a national organisation, with the aim to help people change the direction of their lives, grow as individuals and live life to its full potential. In Manchester, we offer support with harm reduction, needle exchange, housing, criminal justice, employment, education & training and homeless outreach. We have links with other services, including a smoking addiction service also under the Change Grow Live umbrella, called Be Smoke Free, and we offer a service which works specifically with young people, called Eclypse. We work with Emerging Futures and Acorn to deliver our psychosocial intervention groups and after-treatment care, and LGBT Foundation to provide specialist support related to LGBTQ+ issues for those in treatment. 

Change Grow Live's teams work in partnership with service users to assess their requirements and to plan individual treatment plans and support that will help service users to address their problems and achieve their personal goals.

We provide a full range of treatment and recovery interventions for people who require services for their drug or alcohol use. We do this by providing:

- Initial assessment to work out what support will benefit you
- Brief interventions (including harm reduction advice and support over the phone)
- Medically assisted treatment (MAT)
- Support sessions with recovery coordinators and engagement workers – one-to-one and in small groups
- Second opinions when requested by a GP
- Community detox
- Referral for in-patient detox
- Links to rehab clinics
- Peer Support groups – informal drop-ins, and structured group programmes
- Health assessments
- Blood-borne virus (BBV) tests and treatment - HIV, Hep B and Hep C
- Hep B vaccinations
- Needle Syringe Programmes (AKA needle exchange)

We also deliver free online training to professionals on topics related to drug & alcohol use, which you can find on our Eventbrite page:   https://www.eventbrite.co.uk/cc/adult-drug-alcohol-training-for-professionals-2132019
Monday to Friday, 9am – 5pm. Some evening openings available – please ring 0161 823 6306 for details
Manchester

We take referrals from any source as long as they’re with the person’s consent. Clients can also self refer to the service.

Please complete online referral form:  https://www.changegrowlive.org/manchester/referrals

Catch 22's specialist service aims to increase young people’s engagement in diversionary activities that support reductions in the use of substances, and promote sexual health and positive health choices. Early intervention, prevention and resilience building activities are offered along with the direct provision of specialist substance misuse treatment for young people aged up to 24. The team builds relationships with young people that seek to increase their engagement in diversionary pursuits such as health based activities and football, supporting the reduction in the use of substances, promoting sexual health and positive healthy choices.

Support includes:
• comprehensive assessment and specialist care
• planned one-to-one support and treatment interventions
• alcohol, drugs and sex and relationships education workshops for young people
• consultancy and training for professionals working with young people using and/or at risk of using substances, either in-house or on a multi-delegate basis

Metrics.ElementText:
River Young People Support Service is a free and confidential service supporting children and young people under 25 in Liverpool who are affected by their own or someone else’s drug or alcohol use.

We work with young people in a way that suits them—whether in-person, over the phone, or online. Our team also provides advice and support for parents and professionals working with young people in Liverpool.

We provide:
-  Friendly, non-judgmental support tailored to your needs.  
-  Flexible appointments — we can meet at our hub, your school, college, or another place you feel comfortable.  
-  Confidentiality — we’ll keep your information private unless there's a risk of harm to you or someone else.  
-  Support for families and professionals — helping parents and carers talk to their children about drugs and alcohol.  

You don’t need to be dependent on drugs or alcohol to use our service — we’re here for anyone looking for support.

Our CYP services are community based. Please call us on 0151 706 9747 and we will meet you at a venue that is comfortable for you.
Monday - Friday 9am - 5pm - If these hours don’t work for you, let us know - we can often arrange sessions outside these times.
Liverpool

You can get support from our service by making a referral.  
A referral is a form that gives us the information we need to support you.  
You can refer yourself or someone else to the service by:  
- Filling out our online referral form:  https://www.changegrowlive.org/liverpool-yp/referrals  
- Calling us at contact number 0151 706 9747

Metrics.ElementText:
Beacon offers support, information and guidance for anyone in Lincolnshire affected by someone else’s drug or alcohol use.

We recognise the wider impact that the use of substances can have on family and friends, and our team are here to listen to how it’s affecting you in a safe, confidential environment.

We offer open, honest support and advice and have a network of people in similar circumstances that we can connect you with, so know that you are not alone.

Our aim is to equip you with the knowledge, tools and emotional resilience needed to navigate the impact of substance use and focus on your wellbeing. The service is free and entirely non-judgemental, and you can choose the level of support you’d like us to provide.
Monday to Friday 9am - 5pm
Lincolnshire
Self referral or via other agency

Metrics.ElementText:
The Bridge Project is a well-established and vibrant local charity located in the heart of the multi-cultural city of Bradford. 

We provide outreach services to people experiencing the effects of deprivation and health inequalities. Our mission is to empower people experiencing multiple barriers to achieve positive change. 

Co-development is at the heart of our offer. We provide a responsive personalised service to each person who consents and engages with Bridge services. The service provided is curated with a named navigator worker and is not led by service targets.

Our purpose is to help you decide what you would like to change and to support you in achieving your goals.

Services 
We support individuals, families, partners, and communities to improve lives in a sustainable way, recognising that solutions are often multi-faceted and require support to address a range of issues, such as substance misuse, sustaining recovery, homelessness, offending, domestic abuse, sex working, risk-taking behaviours, housing and housing support, physical and/or mental health, and employment.

Approach 
Our staff deliver the Navigator Model of Care, that uses a named navigator to deliver continuous one-to-one professional and practical support, treatment, and advocacy. We support people over extended periods, developing trusting relationships.

Please telephone to check opening times of individual services as there may be slight variations but in general our core hours are:  
Monday 9.30am – 5.30pm, Tuesday 9.30am – 7pm, Wednesday 9.30am – 5.30pm, Thursday 9.30am – 4pm, Friday 9.30am – 5.30pm
Bradford District

Services – Call the office on 01274 723 863 or visit our online ‘Services’ page - https://thebridgeproject.org.uk/services/ - for more information about what we can support with.
Alternatively, you can email - info@thebridgeproject.org.uk and your enquiry will be shared with the most appropriate member of the team

Outreach - Primarily a Monday to Friday outreach service.   Place based - We also offer a place-based Wellbeing Reconnect Centre located at 35 Salem Street in the heart of Bradford. The Centre provides the people we support within with indoor and outdoor space to meet their worker and use personal hygiene facilities and a small kitchen.

The Matrix service helps young people in South Tyneside with substance-related needs through assessments and planned interventions. It is designed to meet the different needs of children,  offering both outreach and centre-based appointments.

Support offered includes:  
• Advice and information for young people and their families  
• Drug and alcohol awareness  
• Support into other health services such as mental/physical health and social care  
• Psychosocial support for social and educational needs  
• Exploring triggers for use and self-help strategies  
• Harm reduction and relapse prevention  
• Safeguarding and risk management  
• Access to sexual health services and condoms 

The team works with other services and partners to address the overall needs of young people and their families.
Monday to Thursday: 9am - 5pm, Friday: 9am - 4.30pm.  Out of hours appointments can be arranged if required.
South Tyneside
Contact us on 0191 4975637 or drop in and see us, you don't need an appointment.

Metrics.ElementText:
Change Grow Live Manchester work with anyone looking to make positive changes related to drug & alcohol use. We approach treatment with an open mind, free from judgement. If your goals don't include treatment and recovery, but you do want to reduce the harmful impacts of drug & alcohol use, we can help with this too.  

Change Grow Live are a national organisation, with the aim to help people change the direction of their lives, grow as individuals and live life to its full potential. In Manchester, we offer support with harm reduction, needle exchange, housing, criminal justice, employment, education & training and homeless outreach. We have links with other services, including a smoking addiction service also under the Change Grow Live umbrella, called Be Smoke Free, and we offer a service which works specifically with young people, called Eclypse. We work with Emerging Futures and Acorn to deliver our psychosocial intervention groups and after-treatment care, and LGBT Foundation to provide specialist support related to LGBTQ+ issues for those in treatment. 

Change Grow Live's teams work in partnership with service users to assess their requirements and to plan individual treatment plans and support that will help service users to address their problems and achieve their personal goals.

We provide a full range of treatment and recovery interventions for people who require services for their drug or alcohol use. We do this by providing:

- Initial assessment to work out what support will benefit you
- Brief interventions (including harm reduction advice and support over the phone)
- Medically assisted treatment (MAT)
- Support sessions with recovery coordinators and engagement workers – one-to-one and in small groups
- Second opinions when requested by a GP
- Community detox
- Referral for in-patient detox
- Links to rehab clinics
- Peer Support groups – informal drop-ins, and structured group programmes
- Health assessments
- Blood-borne virus (BBV) tests and treatment - HIV, Hep B and Hep C
- Hep B vaccinations
- Needle Syringe Programmes (AKA needle exchange)

We also deliver free online training to professionals on topics related to drug & alcohol use, which you can find on our Eventbrite page:   https://www.eventbrite.co.uk/cc/adult-drug-alcohol-training-for-professionals-2132019
Monday to Friday, 9am – 5pm. Some evening openings available – please ring 0161 823 6306 for details
Manchester

We take referrals from any source as long as they’re with the person’s consent. Clients can also self refer to the service.

Please complete online referral form:  https://www.changegrowlive.org/manchester/referrals

Services.ServiceName: Drug misuse - support for family and friends

Metrics.ElementText:
Foundations under 21s service offers a bespoke outreach service for anyone who wants to make changes to their drug or alcohol use, learn more about substances or become abstinent.

We work with you to create a care plan that addresses your needs and will work alongside you to meet your goals. 

We can help you to learn what other services there are in your community, who could help you.
 
Foundations also offers support for those who are affected by someone else’s use. If you are a young person parent care giver or family member Foundations has specific dedicated support for you. This service covers the whole of Suffolk and you do not have to be living with the person who is using drugs or alcohol to access support. 

We also work in close partnership with Iceni so if your needs may be better met by Iceni then we will make this happen. Making sure to keep you informed and empowered. 

If you or someone you know, wants to discuss how we can help you - then you can contact ruth.lee@turning-point.co.uk  or call 0300 123 0872.

9-5 Monday to Friday  

The team work your sessions around your availability and so can offer early mornings or evenings.
Suffolk
If you want to make a referral then you can call 0300 123 0872 or go to https://www.turning-point.co.uk/support-we-offer/young-people and complete the on line form.

Foundations is an outreach service and so we do not have a base – we see you wherever is best for you. But if you need to send us post – then send it to:  Sanderson House, 17-19 Museum Street, Ipswich, Suffolk, IP1 1HE

Metrics.ElementText:
WithYou is a charity providing young people with free, confidential and non-judgemental support with alcohol or drugs. We work with people on their own goals, whether that’s getting a bit of advice, cutting down alcohol or drug use or stopping completely. We give people support in a way that’s right for them either face to face in their local service, community or online. We’re here to help you - you can tell us as little or as much as you want. 

You can also talk to us if you’re worried about someone else’s drug or alcohol use, rather than your own.

This service is for you if:

- you’re under 18

WithYou is a charity providing young people with free, confidential and non-judgemental support with alcohol or drugs. We work with people on their own goals, whether that’s getting a bit of advice, cutting down alcohol or drug use or stopping completely. We give people support in a way that’s right for them either face to face in their local service, community or online. We’re here to help you - you can tell us as little or as much as you want. 

You can also talk to us if you’re worried about someone else’s drug or alcohol use, rather than your own.

This service is for you if:

- you’re under 18

- you’re worried about either your drug or alcohol use, or someone else’s.

Horizons is here to provide you with options around your drug and alcohol use. Whether you want to quit entirely, reduce your use, or learn how to be safer when using drugs and alcohol, we can support you. We also provide support to those affected by someone else’s substance use. 

We take pride in offering a safe, inclusive, and easily accessible service for everyone. Whether you’re reaching out to a drug and alcohol service for the first time or are a regular visitor, you’ll find it simple to access the resources, information, and treatment you need. 

Horizons offer: 
·	Advice and information 
·	One to one support 
·	Group workshops 
·	Support around any substance including alcohol 
·	Specific support for women and people who identify as LGBTQIA+  
·	Services for Young People  
·	Access to a variety of treatment options 
·	Free access to the opioid overdose reversal medication, naloxone 
·	Free access to a range of clean injecting equipment, condoms and more
Monday to Friday 9am - 5pm, Saturday 9:30am – 1pm
Bristol
Self referral or via other agency

GsdServices.ServiceName: Alcohol addiction - support for family and friends

Metrics.ElementText:
WithYou is a charity providing free, confidential and non-judgemental support with alcohol or drugs. We work with people on their own goals, whether that’s getting a bit of advice, cutting down alcohol or drug use or stopping completely. We give people support in a way that’s right for them either face to face in their local service, community or online. Phone us or use our online chat to speak to one of our trained experts. We’re here to help you - you can tell us as little or as much as you want. 

You can also talk to us if you’re worried about someone else’s drug or alcohol use, rather than your own.

This service is for you if:

- you’re over 18
- living in Redcar and Cleveland
- you’re worried about either your drug or alcohol use, or someone else’s.

Metrics.ElementText:
The address listed on this page is the location of the local screening service office, not a screening clinic.

The service delivers diabetic eye screening in a variety of locations throughout the area, including GP surgeries, hospitals and optician practices.

All people aged 12 and over with diabetes (type 1 and 2) are offered annual eye screening appointments.

 The only exceptions are people with diabetic eye disease who are already under the care of an ophthalmology specialist.

 The screening test usually takes around 30 minutes. Screening does not replace regular eye examinations and it is important to attend both.

Free and confidential advice and information for people in Herefordshire, including young people (11-17), young adults (18-24) and adults (25+), families and carers, and veterans. We have hubs in Hereford, Leominster and Ross-on-Wye, with satellites in Ledbury, Kington and Bromyard. We also provide outreach support via our recovery vehicle (Lance).

We offer a range of treatment options, including Motivational Interviewing (MI), Motivational Enhancement Therapy (MET), pathways for non-dependent and dependent alcohol users, non-opiate users, and opiate users (including Opiate Substitute Treatment, OST), and evidence-based psychosocial programmes (in person and online). We also offer harm reduction advice, needle syringe provision (NSP), and overdose awareness including naloxone/nyxoid (opiate overdose reversal drug). We offer assessments within 5 working days, with access to Introduction to Treatment (ITT) sessions to support engagement and referrals to other support services, including Individual Placement Support (IPS) to access employment. We work with service users to design a personalised care plan to meet their needs and promote service user involvement, with peer mentors and lived-experience workers to support recovery check-ins and aftercare.
Monday 9.30am-5pm, Tuesday 9.30am-7pm, Wednesday 1.30pm-5pm, Thursday 9.30am-5pm, Friday 9.30am-5pm
Herefordshire
Self referrals and professional referrals can be made via our website. Self referrals can also be made by calling the service or dropping in during opening times.

Services.ServiceName: Mental health services for alcohol addiction

Metrics.ElementText:
Eclypse is a free and confidential service for young people aged 25 and under in Manchester. We provide support for anyone who is concerned about their own or somebody else’s drug or alcohol use. Our friendly team is on hand to provide advice and tailored support plans to help you achieve your goals. We’re a confidential service, which means we won’t inform anyone of your involvement with us, unless there was a risk of harm to yourself or somebody else. We work in a way that suits you – that might be having appointments over the phone, in-person at our base or your place of choosing, or online via Zoom. 

Eclypse provide access to treatment (drugs/alcohol) and offer holistic support to children, young people and families.  Support can include vaping cessation, sexual health advice, education and training, and employment for 18-24 year olds, stress and anxiety management, improving self-esteem and lots more. Our Family Team work with children affected by parental/family substance misuse to promote resilience and family unity. We can also signpost support for people concerned about a young person’s drug/alcohol use, as we understand the difficulties this can bring to people of any age.

Eclypse will work with any young person living in the Manchester City Council borough, or going to school in the Manchester borough if they want to have appointments at school. There are similar services on offer in neighbouring areas of Salford, Trafford, Rochdale, Oldham and other Greater Manchester areas.

Eclypse also offer groupwork programmes and can deliver bespoke professional training. See our Eventbrite page for online training sessions we have coming up, which cover varied topics related to drugs, alcohol and young people in Manchester, aimed at professionals working within relevant areas.
Monday to Friday 9am - 5pm
Manchester

Accessing Eclypse’s support and advice is easy, and we accept both self and professional referrals. You can call or email using the contact details above, or fill in our short online referral form here - https://www.changegrowlive.org/manchester/referrals. We aim to get back to you within 48 hours.
Make sure to follow us on our socials! We’re @eclypsemanchester on Instagram and @ManchesterEclypse on Facebook!

We also offer harm reduction advice, needle syringe provision (NSP), and overdose awareness including naloxone/nyxoid (opiate overdose reversal drug). We offer assessments within 5 working days, with access to Introduction to Treatment (ITT) sessions to support engagement and referrals to other support services, including Individual Placement Support (IPS) to access employment. We work with service users to design a personalised care plan to meet their needs and promote service user involvement, with peer mentors and lived-experience workers to support recovery check-ins and aftercare.

Services.ServiceName: Mental health services for drug misuse

Metrics.ElementText:
Eclypse is a free and confidential service for young people aged 25 and under in Manchester. We provide support for anyone who is concerned about their own or somebody else’s drug or alcohol use. Our friendly team is on hand to provide advice and tailored support plans to help you achieve your goals. We’re a confidential service, which means we won’t inform anyone of your involvement with us, unless there was a risk of harm to yourself or somebody else. We work in a way that suits you – that might be having appointments over the phone, in-person at our base or your place of choosing, or online via Zoom. 

Eclypse provide access to treatment (drugs/alcohol) and offer holistic support to children, young people and families.  Support can include vaping cessation, sexual health advice, education and training, and employment for 18-24 year olds, stress and anxiety management, improving self-esteem and lots more. Our Family Team work with children affected by parental/family substance misuse to promote resilience and family unity. We can also signpost support for people concerned about a young person’s drug/alcohol use, as we understand the difficulties this can bring to people of any age.

Eclypse will work with any young person living in the Manchester City Council borough, or going to school in the Manchester borough if they want to have appointments at school. There are similar services on offer in neighbouring areas of Salford, Trafford, Rochdale, Oldham and other Greater Manchester areas.

Eclypse also offer groupwork programmes and can deliver bespoke professional training. See our Eventbrite page for online training sessions we have coming up, which cover varied topics related to drugs, alcohol and young people in Manchester, aimed at professionals working within relevant areas.
Monday to Friday 9am - 5pm
Manchester

Accessing Eclypse’s support and advice is easy, and we accept both self and professional referrals. You can call or email using the contact details above, or fill in our short online referral form here - https://www.changegrowlive.org/manchester/referrals. We aim to get back to you within 48 hours.
Make sure to follow us on our socials! We’re @eclypsemanchester on Instagram and @ManchesterEclypse on Facebook!

NHS Cardiovascular Disease (CVD) Health Checks – Outreach
 
A free NHS Health Check is a quick and simple way to check your overall health and help you take action to reduce your risk of developing serious conditions such as heart disease stroke diabetes kidney disease and dementia.
 
Our practitioners will measure your blood pressure take your height and weight measurements check your cholesterol and blood glucose levels. They will also discuss your lifestyle. From these checks you will be given a risk score and that indicates the likelihood of having a cardiovascular event in the next 10 years.  They will help you understand your results and what they mean and provide advice and support on staying healthy. The practitioner will also refer or signpost you to other services if needed.
 
The whole appointment takes 30 minutes so if you are aged 40-74 a resident in Somerset AND / OR registered with a Somerset GP have not had an NHS Health Check already in the past 5 years and have no pre-existing conditions or on certain types of medication you are eligible for a health check!
 
The health checks are currently taking place across Somerset in Wells Yeovil Chard Glastonbury Taunton Langport libraries and at the SHAPE Mendip Council Offices. Details of locations and booking links can be found here: Health Check locations . There will be other locations added in the future.
 
You can book online to ensure your check is booked or you can drop in.
www.nhshealthchecks@somerset.gov.uk

Metrics.ElementText: Look Good Feel Better is a UK based cancer support charity and part of an affiliation operating in 27 countries worldwide. It is the only cancer support charity offering support to women, men and young adults to combat the visible and emotional side-effects of their treatment. Their workshops are normally offered in over 140 hospitals and cancer centres across the UK and to-date has supported over 180,000 people living with cancer. During the current pandemic, the charity has diversified to successfully offer virtual workshops and is in the process of returning to face-to-face sessions. Look Good Feel Better’s group workshops, hosted by trained experts, help people combat the visible side effects of their cancer treatment from hair and eyebrow loss to brittle nails, body confidence, gentle exercise and dry skin. Each session provides participants with a safe, welcoming, and fun environment to learn new skills and techniques. Most importantly, they also provide a vital opportunity to chat, share experiences and feel supported at such a challenging time. If you would like to find out more information about Look Good Feel Better, please visit their website https://lookgoodfeelbetter.co.uk/.

Metrics.ElementText:
The Royal College of Podiatry is the professional body for podiatrists in the UK, setting academic and clinical standards, promoting research and education, and raising awareness of foot health. 
Podiatrists are regulated professionals who are experts in assessing, diagnosing, and treating conditions, injuries, diseases, and traumas of the foot and lower limb. They prevent, manage, and correct foot irregularities, relieve pain, treat infection, and keep people of all ages mobile and active. 
Podiatrists (also known as chiropodists) are regulated by the Health and Care Professions Council (HCPC) and work across both the NHS and independent/private sectors.
While certain NHS treatments are fully funded based on specific local medical criteria, independent and private podiatry services are typically fee-paying unless otherwise specified.
Throughout their careers, the College supports podiatrists to deliver high-quality foot and lower-limb care and to continue developing their skills.
This is a Practising Surgery

Metrics.ElementText: Look Good Feel Better is a UK based cancer support charity and part of an affiliation operating in 27 countries worldwide. It is the only cancer support charity offering support to women, men and young adults to combat the visible and emotional side-effects of their treatment. Their workshops are normally offered in over 140 hospitals and cancer centres across the UK and to-date has supported over 180,000 people living with cancer. During the current pandemic, the charity has diversified to successfully offer virtual workshops and is in the process of returning to face-to-face sessions. Look Good Feel Better’s group workshops, hosted by trained experts, help people combat the visible side effects of their cancer treatment from hair and eyebrow loss to brittle nails, body confidence, gentle exercise and dry skin. Each session provides participants with a safe, welcoming, and fun environment to learn new skills and techniques. Most importantly, they also provide a vital opportunity to chat, share experiences and feel supported at such a challenging time. If you would like to find out more information about Look Good Feel Better, please visit their website https://lookgoodfeelbetter.co.uk/.
